sections.COMMENTS:
The Calabrian Arc stretches SW-NE for about 300 km between the eastern side of Sicily and the Taranto Gulf and then bends abruptly to NW and carries on as a continental collision between the Apennines and the Adria plate. The subduction of oceanic crust of the Africa plate occurs only in the southernmost portion of the arc, about 200 km long.
The Calabrian subduction system includes a SE-verging accretionary wedge extended over the Ionian Sea for about 200 km. Recent interpretations (Merlini et al., 2000; Finetti, 2005; Minelli and Faccenna, 2010; Polonia et al., 2011) of seismic lines revealed its internal structure. It has two distinct lobes, the Eastern lobe and Western lobe, affected by large splay faults deemed to be potentially seismogenic (Polonia et al., 2011, 2012). They reach the subduction plane at a depth of 8-12 km. Geodetic data indicate a shortening rate of 5 mm/y across the entire accretionary wedge (Devoti et al., 2008). Slip rate values are assigned in order to account for geodetic data and are equally partitioned among the mapped structures.
